course_name_original: Basics of measurements and exploitation diagnostics in electric power systems
course_name_en: Basics of measurements and exploitation diagnostics in electric power systems
prerequisites: The module concerns the presentation of the main groups and types of measurements performed in the electric power industry and related issues - scope, methods, measuring devices, purpose.

learning_outcomes.text: Knows and understands the relationship between physical phenomena occurring in electrical power devices and the quantities measured during operational measurements.
Knows the basic hazards associated with working on electrical power devices and related health and safety regulations.
Knows the methods for measuring electrical and non-electrical quantities that are measured during diagnostic and operational measurements discussed in the module.
Knows and understands the importance of assessing and limiting exposures generated by electrical power devices.
Knows current development trends regarding measurement issues in electrical power engineering.
Knows the requirements and recommendations of standards and legal acts related to physical quantities and their measurement methods discussed in the module.
Is able to use literature sources when solving technical problems.
Is able to cooperate during measurement work in a team.
Is able to perform measurements in a planned manner and analyze their results.
Is able to properly select the method and measuring instrument for the measurement task.
Is able to prepare a report on the work performed and present it in various forms.
Is able to apply health and safety rules in practice.
Understands the need for continuous learning and familiarization with new measurement methods and standard recommendations.
Understands the necessity of minimizing the impact of electrical power devices on the environment.
Is aware of the responsibility for their own work and the safety of others dependent on their actions and decisions.
Is able to assess and explain the environmental aspects of the impact of electrical power devices.

syllabus_topics: Laboratory class topics: 1. Measurements of electric and magnetic fields 50Hz – basics. 2. Measurements of electric and magnetic fields 50Hz under transmission lines. 3. Measurements of voltages, currents, power and energy in an electrical substation. 4. Measurements of static earth resistance and soil resistivity. 5. Measurements of dynamic (impulse) earth resistance. 6. Measurement of radioelectric disturbances in the vicinity of HV equipment. 7. Location of faults in cable lines. 8. Measurements of noise level from electrical equipment in the HV laboratory. 9. Pyrometric measurements during inspections of electrical installations and equipment. 10. Testing of protective equipment.

Lecture topics: 1. Purpose, scope and organization of measurements in electrical power engineering. Main groups and types of operational measurements performed in electrical power engineering. Scope of measurements, planned and ad-hoc operational and diagnostic measurements. Workplace hazards. Basic health and safety rules. Live working: methods, procedures, protective equipment. 2. Basic electrical and non-electrical quantities in diagnostic measurements in operation. Overview of electrical and non-electrical quantities measured in operation. Measurement methods, transducers and measuring instruments used. Insulation resistance measurements. Classical and unconventional instrument transformers. Disturbances during measurements and methods of their elimination. 3. Field exposures from electrical power devices. Impact of electrical power devices on the environment and field hazards in the workplace. Analysis of the impact of E and H fields, methods of limiting them. Classification and division of E-M field impact zones, normative requirements, significance and impact of standardization and legal regulations on operational work. 4. Measurements of E and H field strength in the vicinity of electrical power facilities. Methods of measuring E and H field strength. Construction and properties of basic types of 50Hz electric field meters, dipole probe and Miller probe, scope of application, measurement methodology. 50Hz magnetic field measurements, measured quantities, measurement methods, construction of meters. Factors affecting the accuracy of 50Hz electromagnetic field measurements. 5. Radioelectric disturbances from electrical power devices. Selected issues of electromagnetic compatibility. Conducted and radiated disturbances. Mechanisms of RIV radioelectric disturbance generation. Characteristics of RIV disturbances generated by power lines and stations. Normative requirements. Construction of instruments for measuring radioelectric disturbances. Measurement methodology. New RIV measurement methods used in the operation of overhead transmission lines. 6. Operational measurements at electrical substations. Measurements of basic electrical quantities at electrical substations. Methods and systems for measuring voltages and currents used in electrical power engineering. Power and energy measurements, examples of solutions used in practice. 7. Noise measurements emitted by electrical power devices. Noise – definitions, measured quantities, methods and measuring instruments. Mechanisms of noise generation in various types of electrical power devices and facilities: overhead lines, transformers and wind farms. Methods of reducing noise from electrical power devices. Normative requirements and legal regulations concerning noise emission levels. 8. Measurements of soil resistivity and earthing resistance. Classification and purpose of earthing. Electrical properties of soils. Measurements of soil resistivity, methods, measuring instruments. Static and dynamic earthing resistance, measurement methods, measuring instruments, measurement methodology. 9. Operational measurements and fault location in cable lines. Types of tests performed on cables in operation. Detection and location of faults in cable lines: classification of methods, sectional, preliminary and precise location. Measurements of insulation resistance and continuity of cable cores. Methods and measuring instruments used. 10. Recording of transient waveforms in fault conditions. Transient waveforms in electrical power systems, causes, parameters. Methods of disturbance recording, requirements for disturbance recording instruments, standardized data formats. Analysis of transient waveforms. 11. Development trends in measurements in electrical power engineering. New technical solutions for measurement systems in electrical power engineering, IED devices. Digitalization, remote measurements, transmission and exchange of information.

assessment_methods.method: Lectures (Activity during classes, Execution of laboratory classes, Test, Report, Oral answer, Completion of laboratory classes)
Laboratory classes (Activity during classes, Execution of laboratory classes, Test, Report, Involvement in teamwork, Presentation, Oral answer, Completion of laboratory classes)

assessment_rules: Positive passing of laboratory classes and a final test are required for lectures. Participation in laboratory classes and their positive passing during the test are required for lab classes. Completion of the module is possible after passing all laboratory classes.
